sources.title: CTRE: compile-time parsing and validation of regex literals
sources.sections_read: README capabilities, basic API, supported compilers
sources.confirmed: CTRE accepts static regex patterns through C++ templates and supports matching, searching and captures. Its current interface depends on modern C++ language features.
sources.limits: This is later evidence from C++; its template mechanism is not directly transferable to Rust, and shifting work into compilation creates a build-time and generated-code tradeoff. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: RE2: automata engine and matching API
sources.sections_read: README design goals, syntax and C++ matching API
sources.confirmed: RE2 supplies whole-string and substring matching with captures, memory budgets and a non-backtracking implementation. It omits backreferences and look-around.
sources.limits: C++ reuse requires an integration boundary; omitted backreferences and look-around are a feature tradeoff, and predictable matching time is an optional benefit rather than an input requirement. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: Original PCRE: Perl-style C regex library
sources.confirmed: The tool supplied a rewritten summary of the redirected PCRE site, describing Perl-style matching and native/POSIX APIs. It distinguishes original PCRE from PCRE2.
sources.limits: A wrapper adds native build and maintenance obligations; the original engine uses backtracking, and the current site marks it unmaintained while distinguishing the later PCRE2 line. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: Rust regex crate: runtime patterns with reusable compiled objects
sources.sections_read: README usage, capture iteration, lazy reuse, UTF-8/byte APIs
sources.confirmed: The Rust crate offers string matching and captures, recommends reusing compiled patterns, and exposes separate UTF-8 and arbitrary-byte interfaces.
sources.limits: The reviewed API is current and not established by the cutoff; lazy initialization is runtime work, not compile-time compilation, and the engine omits look-around and backreferences. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: Oniguruma: configurable-encoding regex engine
sources.sections_read: README overview, encoding support and project status
sources.confirmed: Oniguruma allows a character encoding per pattern and combines features from multiple regex dialects. The live repository states that the project ended in April 2025.
sources.limits: The encoding surface and native integration need an explicit Rust policy; the reviewed repository ended development in 2025, and not every current feature is established for its 2013 version. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: TRE: POSIX-style matching with approximate-search extensions
sources.sections_read: Introduction; approximate matching; POSIX conformance; memory and encoding sections
sources.confirmed: TRE offers POSIX-style matching with optional edit-distance matching and separate compilation/execution. Its documentation states caveats for backreferences and incomplete collation support.
sources.limits: Fuzzy matching is beyond the minimum goal; backreferences alter performance behavior, some collation features are missing, and historical/current licenses and APIs must be checked per chosen version. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C17.json.

sources.title: Ragel: regular-language compilation into generated state machines
